criteria.title: Encrypted-request relay discovery is explicit
criteria.statement: The browser must derive encrypted-request relay URLs only from `nostr.browser_encrypted_request_relays` and must not treat `nostr.browser_relays` as encrypted-request relays.

criteria.title: Encrypted transport availability is gated by system discovery
criteria.statement: Sensitive browser stores must fail before publish when system discovery does not advertise both a Bahia service pubkey and encrypted-request relay URLs.

criteria.title: Encrypted requests are constructed for the Bahia service pubkey
criteria.statement: The browser must build kind `5980` request events, encrypt the envelope to the Bahia service pubkey, and include `['p', service_pubkey]` plus `['encrypted', 'bahia-encrypted-v1']` tags.

criteria.title: Publish success requires at least one accepted OK
criteria.statement: The browser transport must treat encrypted request publish as successful only when at least one encrypted-request relay returns an accepted OK, and must surface relay rejection reasons when all relays reject.

criteria.title: Encrypted results are strictly correlated
criteria.statement: The browser must resolve encrypted results only when they match the request event id, requester pubkey, and Bahia service pubkey author, and it must ignore mismatched or spoofed results.

criteria.title: Backend unauthorized and decrypt failures return encrypted terminal errors
criteria.statement: The backend encrypted transport must publish correlated encrypted terminal error results for undecryptable requests and unauthorized requesters, and must not dispatch unauthorized requests to handlers.

criteria.title: Notifications use encrypted operations only
criteria.statement: Notification channel list/create/update/test/delete and log retrieval must execute through encrypted request/result operations rather than direct REST calls in the current web store path.

criteria.title: Terminal encrypted errors surface to callers
criteria.statement: If an encrypted result carries terminal error status, the frontend notification store must surface the backend-provided error message to the caller and local error state.

criteria.title: Sensitive browser traffic stays off public relays
criteria.statement: The encrypted browser transport must not use public browser relay URLs for sensitive request publication or result subscription.

criteria.title: Feature-level browser journey evidence exists
criteria.statement: The slice should have at least one end-to-end browser-level verification path proving the notifications journey on top of the encrypted transport in addition to unit and backend transport tests.

coverage_notes: Current evidence is strongest at unit and backend transport levels.
Selected evidence does not include a notifications browser E2E test, so AC-010 is currently a known gap rather than a passing criterion.
This slice deliberately treats `/api/v1/system/info` as part of the feature contract because the browser cannot safely bootstrap encrypted operations without it.
unresolved_questions: Should AC-010 be upgraded from SHOULD to MUST for release gating?
Should the encrypted operation catalog be versioned/documented per domain as normative API surface?
